start: ^I nearly didn't come in tonight. I stood outside for a few minutes wondering whether I should just go home, but I really didn't want to be there by myself.
^It sounds like being at home alone felt difficult tonight. What happened?
^Well, you're here now. Take your time.
^Sometimes getting out of the house can help after a difficult day.

c-0: ^Yeah... I think being there was making everything feel worse.
c-2: ^Maybe. I think that's partly why I came out.

loss_reveal: ^My aunt died three days ago. Calling her my aunt almost feels strange because she was basically a second mum to me. Everyone keeps asking if I'm okay, and I honestly don't know what I'm supposed to say.
^She sounds like she was much more than just an aunt to you. What was she like?

c-0: ^She really was. She was loud, stubborn, funny... and somehow she always knew when something was wrong with me before I even said anything.
c-1: ^Thank you. I've heard that a lot this week, but I know people mean well.
c-2: ^Yeah. Everything still feels a bit unreal.

funeral_boundary: ^The funeral arrangements have been exhausting too. Everyone wants to talk about dates, flowers, who is travelling... Honestly, I don't really want to talk about any of that right now.
^Of course. We don't have to talk about it.
^Maybe taking a break from the arrangements for a day would help.

c-0: ^Thanks. I think I just needed someone not to ask me another question about the funeral.
c-2: ^Maybe. I don't think I can completely avoid it, but I definitely need a break from thinking about it.

sunday_calls: ^She used to call me every Sunday morning. Sometimes we'd talk for an hour and sometimes for five minutes. Yesterday I picked up my phone because I was going to call her... and then I remembered.
^Those calls were part of your life with her. It must feel strange having that routine suddenly gone.
^Maybe you could write down some of your memories of her while they're still fresh.

c-0: ^Yeah. That's exactly it. It's all the little things that keep catching me off guard.
c-1: ^Actually... that's not a bad idea. There are so many ridiculous stories about her that I don't want to forget.
c-2: ^Every single Sunday. She almost never missed one.

memories: ^She made everything feel safe somehow. Whenever something went wrong, I could call her and she'd listen without immediately telling me what I should do. Everyone around me now is trying so hard to make me feel better.
^So you don't just miss her advice. You miss having someone who would let you talk without trying to fix everything.
^People sometimes don't know what to say when someone is grieving.

c-0: ^Yes. That's exactly it. I don't need somebody to magically make this disappear.
c-1: ^It is. I know everyone is trying their best.
c-2: ^Yeah. I know they're trying to help.

service_moment: ^I haven't really been looking after myself either. I barely ate today, I've hardly slept, and I don't think I've had much to drink since this morning. I came in thinking I'd order something, but now I'm not really sure what I want.

b: ^Water actually sounds good. I didn't realise how thirsty I was until now.
^Yeah, something soft sounds fine. Something simple is probably best tonight.
^I thought alcohol was what I wanted when I walked in. I'm not completely sure that's what I need anymore, though.
^Actually... could we just keep talking for another minute? I think that's helping more than I expected.

evaluate_service: ^Give me another minute. I'm still figuring out what I want.
after_service: ^My mum is taking everything really badly. Everyone keeps saying that I need to be strong for her. I understand why, but sometimes it feels like I'm not allowed to be upset because I'm supposed to be looking after everyone else.
^It sounds like you're carrying your own grief while also feeling responsible for everyone else's. What do you need for yourself right now?
^Maybe somebody else in the family could support your mum for a while so you can take a break.
^That's a lot for one person to carry.

c-0: ^Honestly? I think I just need permission to stop pretending I'm fine, even if it's only for one night.
c-1: ^My sister probably could. I've been trying to do everything myself.

sister_decision: ^My sister actually asked me to stay with her tonight. Part of me wants to because I don't really want to be alone, but another part of me wants my own space. I genuinely don't know what I should do.
^Maybe you could stay with her tonight and see how you feel tomorrow. It doesn't have to be a decision about the whole week.
^You don't have to decide this second.

c-0: ^That actually sounds manageable. One night doesn't feel as overwhelming as thinking about the whole week.
c-1: ^Yeah. Both options feel right and wrong at the same time.
c-2: ^That's true. I suppose I've been treating everything like it needs an answer immediately.

self_judgement: ^Sometimes I feel guilty for even struggling this much. My mum lost her sister, and other people in the family are grieving too. Part of me keeps thinking I should be handling this better.
^It sounds like you're comparing your grief with everyone else's and judging yourself for feeling it differently.
^Grief is difficult for everyone in different ways.
^You don't have to have everything figured out three days after losing someone.

c-0: ^Yeah... I hadn't really thought about it like that. Nobody has actually told me I'm handling it badly. I think I'm putting that pressure on myself.
c-2: ^That's probably true. Three days isn't exactly a long time.

final_reflection: ^You know... when I came in, I thought I needed something that would make me stop feeling sad. But I don't think that's actually possible. Maybe feeling sad isn't the problem.
^It sounds like you didn't need the sadness taken away. You needed somewhere you could feel it without someone trying to change it.
^I'm glad you decided to come in tonight.

c-0: ^Yeah. That's exactly what I needed tonight.

ending: ^I'm still sad, and I know one conversation isn't going to change what happened. But talking about my aunt tonight helped me get some of it out.
^Thanks for giving me somewhere to sit for a while.
